ruling.explanation:
Trip TRP-02837, route-deviation dispute filed by the rider, contested amount $4.50.

Rider, the measured facts are not in dispute. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02837) is clean for policy purposes: 104 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) are not met and the trace is not impaired. It records a trace_distance_km of 13.2. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02837) is METERED with charged_total 19.32 and the booked optimal_distance_km was 10.0.

The decisive point is the drop-off change, which turns the baseline. Your own chat message (EV-CHAT-02837, sent 17:03:32) says you changed the pin, and the trip record (EV-TRIP-02837) shows dropoff_amended_at 17:04:12 with a stored amended_optimal_distance_km of 13.4 and amended_optimal_duration_min of 18.5. POL-RD-05 therefore requires the POL-RD-01 test to be re-run between the amended endpoints, and the baseline becomes the platform's stored re-quote of 13.4 km — I take it as recorded and do not derive a substitute. Against that baseline there is no excess: 13.2 - 13.4 = -0.2 km, which cannot clear POL-RD-01 (excess must exceed 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km absolute). No deviation survives the recomputation and POL-RD-05 directs the outcome to NO_ACTION.

The rider's advocate's booked-baseline figure (excess 3.2 km / 32.0%) is not the operative measure: POL-RD-01 requires establishment and materiality to be judged on the excess REMAINING after any POL-RD-05 adjustment, and the POL-RD-05 adjustment removes it. That claim is answered and outweighed by the amended baseline.

Consequences: POL-RD-02 does not run, so no distance-or-time refund issues (had it run on the booked baseline the arithmetic would be charged_total 19.32 - recomputed_fare 16.02 = 3.30; neither that nor the 4.50 contested amount is payable, because no deviation is established). POL-RD-04 is unavailable and I say so: the instruction meets POL-RD-04(a) and (b), but chat_message.waypoint_hint is null, so the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run on this record and the clause is unavailable; it is not needed, because POL-RD-05 resolves the case. POL-RD-09: no ERP gantry and no airport surcharge line was charged, so there is no billing-integrity correction and no POL-RD-09(4) referral. POL-RD-06: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d 237 (ratio 0.004), so no repeat-deviation pattern, no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral. POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so no corroboration uplift applies. POL-RD-04's compensation limb does not fire either: the billed distance (13.2 km) is not less than the trace (13.2 km), so there is no unbilled-kilometre shortfall and no driver compensation.

The driver's account ('the rider moved the drop-off pin during the trip') is consistent with the chat log and the amendment timestamp; it is not a traffic-cause defence, no party invoked POL-RD-03, and the MISSING advisory (EV-ADVIS-02837-01, weight 0.0) therefore has no bearing on this case. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: confidence is well above 0.70, all trip identifiers and timestamps agree, the trace is unimpaired, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a cited-and-missing artifact, no refund exceeds 150.00, and there is no mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength.

Confidence: the finding rests on EV-TRIP-02837 and EV-GPS-02837, both at weight 1.0, with EV-CHAT-02837 (also 1.0) corroborating the amendment; the cap is 1.0 and I set confidence at 0.95. No money moves, so the monetary effect is zero — below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of 8.00. This ruling is provisional; either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04, and the appeal route is set out in the notice.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties largely agree on the facts that decide this case, and so do I.

Trip TRP-02837 was booked from Blk 55 Lengkok Bahru to Blk 112 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4 (original pin) with a platform optimal route of 10.0 km. During the trip the rider sent an in-app message at 17:03:32 — 'actually can you drop me at the other building, i changed the pin' — and the trip record then shows the drop-off point amended at 17:04:12. That is a drop-off relocation governed by POL-RD-05, which requires the deviation test to be re-run against the optimal route between the amended endpoints. The platform stored that figure on the trip record: trip_record.amended_optimal_distance_km = 13.4 km (with amended_optimal_duration_min = 18.5 min). The governing actual distance is the trace figure, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 13.2 km, which POL-RD-01 requires over the rounded trip_record copy. Excess = 13.2 − 13.4 = −0.2 km, i.e. the trip was driven within the amended optimal route. No deviation survives the POL-RD-05 recomputation, and POL-RD-05 directs NO_ACTION where it does not.

The rider's alternative reading — use the 10.0 km booked figure, giving a 3.2 km / 32.0% excess and a POL-RD-02 refund of $3.30 (charged_total $19.32 less recomputed_fare $16.02) — is rejected. POL-RD-02 runs only once a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, and POL-RD-05 removes the deviation before POL-RD-02 is reached. The rider moved the pin; the additional distance answers the rider's own request, not a driver default.

The GPS trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 104 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, max_gap_sec 0.0 and no straight-line jump over 500 m, so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) are not met. Because the trace is unimpaired, no independent corroboration is required, the deviation (were one established) would rest on the trace as measured, and no escalation under POL-RD-10(3) arises.

The rider's chat instruction also satisfies POL-RD-04(a) and (b), but the 200 m corroboration test in POL-RD-04(c) cannot be run because chat_message.waypoint_hint is null; the clause is unavailable on the record (POL-RD-14), and nothing turns on it because POL-RD-05 already governs the amendment. The driver's account that the rider moved the pin is itself corroborated by the chat log and the dropoff_amended_at timestamp, so the driver is not charged with the distance driven to the amended point.

No billing-integrity defect exists: the fare ledger shows no ERP gantry charges and no airport surcharge, and the $19.32 total reconciles to its itemised lines, so POL-RD-09(4) produces neither a refund nor a referral. No repeat-deviation pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 1 (below the 3-flag threshold) and 1/237 completed_trips_90d = 0.004 (below 0.05), so POL-RD-06 does not fire and no driver-conduct referral is made. The rider's profile (deviation_claims_60d = 0, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated = 0) does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift. Profile fields that POL-GEN-01 makes context-only (rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, prior_disputes_filed, prior_deviation_flags) were mentioned only to be disclaimed and were not used as grounds of decision.

No traffic advisory was cited by either party and none is relied on; the missing advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02837-01 (MISSING, weight 0.0) is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction, and under POL-RD-13 it neither supplies an excuse nor escalates anything. No exculpatory clause was invoked against a cited-but-absent artifact.

The result is NO_ACTION: the rider's claim is not supported on this record and the $19.32 charge stands as paid (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The monetary effect is $0.00, below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00. This ruling rests on artifacts at weight 1.0.
